ads.text:
As a mom here, North Carolina, I generally cannot wrap my head around this.
Michael Wattley is running to represent North Carolina in the U.S. in it.
But there's something about his time leading in the North Carolina Republican Party
that I think people need to know about.
Harvey Lee West was accused of sexual crimes involving underage girls.
He ultimately played guilty to 16 counts of indecent liberties with children
and served six years in prison.
Years later,
Michael Watley appointed him to leadership positions
within the North Carolina Republican Party.
But here's what I really can't get past.
Wes says they knew.
He said he was completely open with the party's leadership
about his criminal history.
This wasn't something that came to light until after the fact.
And that's what changes everything for me.
Because if you knew about his past,
why would you want to put him in a position of trust?
I'm raising my kids here.
I care about who represents our state, but I also care about the judgment and character
of the people asking us to trust them.
If this is who Michael Wattley trusts, I simply cannot trust him to represent North
Carolina and the U.S. Senate.
You can learn more about Michael Wattley in Harvey West at MichaelWattleyFacts.com.

Can we talk about how out of touch Susan Collins is
with the actual cost of living in Maine
and what actually matters to us?
Apparently when Maynars are worried about rising prices,
we're supposed to feel better
because road salt got a tax exemption.
But I guess that's what happens
when you haven't hosted a town hall meeting
in over 20 years with your constituents.
And listen, I appreciate a safe road
as much as the next Maynare.
We do get a lot of snow.
I can't keep my house with road salt.
I can't pay my bills with road salt.
Heck, it literally tells you on the bag to wear gloves when handling it, so I definitely
am not putting this on my mashed potatoes.
We're worried about tariffs driving up the cost of groceries, heating oil, child care
and whether or not our paychecks are going to stretch to the end of the month.
We need a senator who understands that reality, unlike Susan Collins, whose net worth has
grown by more than 10 million during her time in office.
Because right now, that disconnect is wild.

ads.text:
The most existential threat currently facing
Iowans is the continuing worsening and degradation of our water resources.
As the situation has worsened and cancer rates have risen despite them falling
on a national level, Iowa's second congressional district rep, Ashley Henson,
has taken actions to make the problem worse.
Cancer rates in Iowa are some of the highest in the entire country.
In her last term, she voted to strip regulations around protections for
sources of drinking water and also voted to defund two separate programs designed to support
access to clean drinking water all while taking $300,000 of contributions from corporate polluters.
This is not a partisan issue. A majority of islands in a recent poll, including 72% of Republicans,
said they were more likely to support a candidate who prioritized clean drinking water.
So it just blows my mind that we have politicians so willing to go so strongly against public sentiment.
So someone please tell Ashley Hinson that she needs to start prioritizing clean drinking water.

We do not need people like him in office here in Texas. Election day is November 3rd, and early voting starts October 19th. I wouldn't even say take my word for it. Look up his record and then go vote because truly us Texans deserve to know who Ken Paxson is.

How does a guy making $153,000 a year
end up owning $9 million of real estate?
Most of us are simply trying to keep one roof over our heads.
But Ken Paxton, our attorney general,
owns 15 properties total.
That includes three luxury properties in Utah
with $1.3 million in mortgages that he did not disclose.
And let's not talk about the ocean view property
he owns in Maui. His own financial
disclosure puts his net worth
between $1 million and $27 million.
Honestly, it's just ridiculous.
And this is far from his first
controversy. Back in 2020,
eight of his own senior staff
members went to law enforcement
saying that he would abuse his office.
And several of them ended up losing
their jobs. Then in 2023,
his own Texas house voted to impeach
him with a vote of
of 121 to 23.
And now he wants to go to the US Senate
and take more power.
We do not need people like him in office here in Texas.
Election day is November 3rd,
and early voting starts October 19th.
I wouldn't even say take my word for it.
Look up his record and then go vote
because truly us Texans deserve to know who Ken Paxson is.

Go vote early because I promise you, the left is.

ads.text:
Did you know that gas is up $1.65 a gallon this year?
On November 3rd, vote for Sean McCain.
While we pay more, congressmen like Bill Heizinga
are increasing their network and turning down
community project funding.
Money can go to roads, our water, and health centers.
And he leaves it all on the table.
McCain has been a Kalamazoo city commissioner,
a state rep, a state senator, and a small business owner.
He's running on lower-end cost and protecting
health care and social security.
General Election is November 3rd.
Make sure you vote for McCann.
C
BILL HUIZENGA
MCCANN HAS BEEN
HENMO
HEALTHCARE
PALD FOR BY AFSCME PEOPLE, AFSOMEPEOPLE ORG.

ads.text:
I don't usually talk politics on this page, but I do think one thing is really important
no matter who you're planning to vote for, please spend a little time researching the people
on your ballot.
Campaign ads and headlines only tell a part of the story.
I always think it's worth looking at things like a candidate's voting record, what policies
they've supported, and whether those decisions line up with what matters most to you.
For example, I was researching Congresswoman Monica Delacruz's record, and I learned
about those on issues like healthcare, food assistance, and tariffs that I personally wanted
to know more about before making a decision.
And those issues did influence my own decision.
She voted for legislation that included cuts to Medicaid and food assistance programs
to issues that affect a lot of everyday Texans.
I also learned that she voted multiple times,
six times actually, to protect Trump's tariffs,
which has contributed to higher costs for Texans.
And these are the kinds of things I think are worth looking into for yourself.
She is not voted for the people of Texas, but wants us to vote for her.
At the end of the day, voting is personal.
but making an informed decision should not be optional.
Do your research, read from multiple sources, ask questions,
and make the choice that aligns with your values.
Let's elect officials who have our best interests at heart,
and please do not forget to vote this election cycle.
Don't forget to vote this
election season!!

ads.text:
Hey, series question. Have you made your plan to vote? Don't sit these midterm elections out.
As a Nevada, your vote will have more impact than ever in deciding some of our most key races.
Right here in Congressional District 2, Teresa Bonita's Thompson is our Democratic candidate,
and she is running on issues that matter to us students, including affordability
and finding jobs after graduation. Head to iBullVote.com to check your voter registration today,
find your nearest polling location, and then send it to your friends and to your group chats.
Voting is simple and easy and we have a location right here on campus, so make
sure to vote and vote early.
serious
Benitez-Thompson
IWillVote.com/NV

federal_scope_evidence.text: Alvarado won't support teacher pensions Clark County teacher: "Sen. Ralph Alvarado refused to pledge his support in defending the teachers' retirement system." Uhr Wincheater Sun I want to thank Sen. Ralph Alvarado for meeting with me, a concerned constituent and teacher in Clark County, and discussing the teachers' pension system March 20 in his office at the Capitol Annex building in Frankfort. When we met, I gave him a petition signed by 292 educators in Clark County in the hope he would agree to our demand that our legislators support the teachers' retirement system in its current structure. Teachers, who are not eligible for Social Security benefits, rely on our pensions as the primary source of income for our retirement. Our pensions are currently under threat because the legislature failed to adequately fund the system.
